study type: Experimental animal study (nonhuman primate model) with in vitro and ex vivo human sample analysis
outcome: Inflammatory cytokines (IL-1beta, TNF-alpha, IL-6, IL-8, CCL2)
cohort: The study included preterm chronically catheterized pregnant pigtail macaques, in vitro human amniocytes, amnion from women with polyhydramnios, and amnion and myometrium from women with twins in early labor.
finding: Uterine overdistention is associated with an inflammatory pulse that precedes and correlates with preterm labor, indicating that inflammation is an early event following mechanical stress on the uterus and leads to preterm labor when the stress is sufficiently great.
cross-section timing: Early labor (for women with twins), or presence of polyhydramnios
gest_age: Preterm (for macaques); implicitly related to preterm birth for human samples analyzed
